jobs.title: Sales Enablement Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Coder is hiring its first Sales Enablement Manager for EMEA, who will sit within our Content & Learning pillar and report directly to the Head of Sales Enablement. You will be the enablement presence for the region, creating and adapting content, building programs, and supporting the EMEA sales team across a diverse set of markets.

This is an individual contributor role for someone who thrives in a build-from-scratch environment, knows how enterprise sales work across EMEA, and can move between content creation, regional training, and cross-functional collaboration without losing momentum. You'll work closely with the global enablement team, Marketing, and Product Marketing while independently owning the regional agenda.

If you're someone who knows that a playbook that works in North America doesn't automatically work in EMEA, loves building things that sales teams actually use, and wants to be the first enablement hire in a region with real room to shape how it's done, this role is for you.

This position follows a hybrid work model. Candidates should be local and able to work from our London office on a regular weekly basis, with scheduling flexibility.

What you’ll do here

  • Create and adapt sales enablement content for EMEA markets playbooks, battlecards, competitive positioning, and training materials that reflect regional buyer dynamics, language nuance, and sales culture

  • Build and deliver onboarding and ongoing training programs for EMEA sales reps, ensuring they ramp quickly and stay current on product and messaging updates

  • Partner closely with Product Marketing and Marketing to translate global messaging and positioning into field-ready content that actually resonates with EMEA buyers. Pushing back constructively when global content needs regional adaptation

  • Work with EMEA sales leadership and SDR leadership to understand what reps need in the field and turn that signal into content and programs that are practical and immediately useful

  • Collaborate with the global Content & Learning team to ensure regional content is consistent with global standards while remaining locally relevant

  • Identify gaps in the EMEA enablement program and proactively build resources to close them

What we’re looking for

  • 2–4 years of experience in sales enablement, content creation, or a revenue-facing role with an EMEA focus

  • Proven ability to create high-quality enablement content independently. You can go from a brief to a finished playbook without hand-holding

  • Strong understanding of EMEA enterprise sales dynamics

  • Comfortable working remotely and autonomously as the sole enablement person in a region. You can set your own priorities and manage up effectively

  • Strong internal collaborator. You know how to consume global messaging, identify where it needs to flex for the region, and work cross-functionally to get it right

  • Excellent communicator in English; additional European language proficiency a plus

  • High ownership, strong judgment, and the ability to own your domain as a P3 individual contributor.

Bonus tacos if you have

  • (Tacos? If you need an ice-breaker, ask how we say thanks by giving tacos!)

  • Background in B2B SaaS, enabling enterprise sales teams

  • Experience enabling sellers in a developer tools, infrastructure, or platform engineering context

  • Familiarity with various sales platforms (Highspot, Nooks, LetterAI)

  • Experience supporting partner or channel sales motions

  • Prior experience as a first or early enablement hire in a region

About Coder

Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com.

Interview process 

We believe that the interview process should be transparent, consistent, and enjoyable. We value your time and hope to complete the interview process in two to four weeks, if schedules allow. Through your interviews, you will meet a mix of individual contributors, managers, and senior leaders.

AI use during the interview process

As an AI company, Coder embraces the use of AI tools, and we want to be transparent about our expectations as you navigate our interview process.

Not permitted: Using AI assistance during conversational interviews.

Permitted: Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly.

Our use of AI in hiring

We use AI tools to help manage our recruitment process efficiently and fairly. Specifically:

  • Ashby and Brainerr help us review inbound applications by surfacing candidates who best match the role requirements we've defined. This tool does not make hiring decisions; it helps our team prioritize which applications to review first.

  • Granola takes notes during our interview calls so our team can focus on the conversation with you.

All hiring decisions are made by humans. Our team reviews applications, conducts interviews, and makes final selections. AI tools assist us but never replace human judgment, and these practices are conducted in compliance with applicable data protection, AI governance, and labor laws. jobs.descriptionHtml:
We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help shape AI governance for developer tooling at Coder. This role sits on our AI Governance team, which builds and maintains two enterprise-grade components of Coder's AI governance stack.

AI Gateway is a centralized LLM gateway that sits between coding agents and providers such as OpenAI or Anthropic, providing organizations with audit trails, token tracking, cost control, and centralized authentication. Agent Firewall wraps those agents with default-deny network policies, controlling which domains and methods they can reach inside workspaces.

This team works across the full stack - from Go backend and React frontend to integrating with LLM provider APIs. Day to day, you'll be shipping features, hardening security boundaries, collaborating with enterprise customers on real-world policy needs, and contributing to Coder's open-source ecosystem.

 

What you'll do here

  • Design and build product features that push the standard for remote development in self-hosted environments

  • Create and improve upon popular open source projects that integrate with VS Code, JetBrains, and other developer tools

  • Champion best practices to both internal team members and external contributors

  • Collaborate with Product and Design teams at Coder, as well as with partners like JetBrains, to execute key product integrations

  • Document the design, implementation, and operations of systems for knowledge sharing within the team

  • Work alongside Customer Success teams to support Coder’s enterprise user base

  • Work with cutting-edge AI technologies to create seamless, painless developer experiences

  • Rapidly iterate from prototype to implementation in a highly adaptive, reactive team environment

     

What we're looking for

  • 8+ years of full-stack experience writing code in a professional setting, with 1+ year(s) writing Go (ideally in current or most recent position)

  • Proficiency in building distributed systems in Go

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Exceptional debugging and troubleshooting skills, and the tenacity to drive a solution to a conclusion

  • You are self-motivated with a creative and analytical mindset

 

Our tech stack

  • Frontend: Typescript, React, Vite

  • Backend: Go, Postgres, GCP, Kubernetes, gRPC

  • Observability: Prometheus, Grafana

  • CI/CD: GitHub Actions

  • General: GitHub, Slack, Discord, Notion

jobs.title: Software Engineer (Enterprise Experience, Backend)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
As a Backend Engineer on Coder's Enterprise Experience team, you'll build the features that help large organizations run Coder in production with confidence. The team owns what administrators and operators need to run Coder well. That covers how it scales, how it's upgraded, how reliably it performs, how it's observed and reported on, how activity is held accountable, and how it's secured.

You'll join a cross-functional team of backend, platform, and QA engineers who own the operator experience end to end. You'll ship features from design through production and partner with product and design to solve real operator problems.

What you'll do here

  • Build features end to end, from a design you write within the team's existing approach through production rollout.

  • Write database migrations that follow the team's patterns for schema compatibility and safe upgrades.

  • Build the observability, reporting, and audit features administrators rely on to see what their deployment is doing.

  • Build features that keep enterprise deployments secure, following the team's security practices.

  • Help investigate and resolve scalability bottlenecks under production-like load, from database access patterns to concurrency in coderd.

  • Help resolve backend issues surfaced by Coder operators and administrators.

  • Document the features you build so a reviewer and the next engineer do not have to decode them.

  • Participate in code reviews, contribute to RFC-style design discussions, and join the on-call rotation.

What we're looking for

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering experience.

  • Professional experience writing and shipping Go.

  • Working understanding of Go's concurrency model, including goroutines, channels, and the sync package.

  • Comfortable with SQL, schema changes, and writing migrations.

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including surfacing blockers and uncertainty early.

  • Solid debugging skills and the persistence to work a problem, and to escalate early when stuck.

  • A self-motivated, analytical engineer who enjoys difficult technical challenges.

Bonus tacos if you have

  • (Tacos? If you need an ice-breaker, ask how we say thanks by giving tacos!)

  • Experience investigating performance under real-world load, including debugging race conditions.

  • Experience with observability, audit, or security features in an enterprise product.

  • Experience with major cloud providers, Kubernetes, and container orchestration.

  • Experience building or operating distributed systems at a meaningful scale.

  • Curiosity about the latest developer tooling.

jobs.title: Field Marketing Manager (NYC)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Developers don’t want more marketing. They want relevance, technical depth, and experiences worth showing up for. As Field Marketing Manager you will help bring Coder’s regional marketing programs to life. You will execute field and ABM programs that build awareness, support sales, and create pipeline across the North American market.

You will work closely with a Senior Marketing Manager, sales, partners, and the broader marketing team. You will coordinate events, activate campaigns, and keep programs moving on time and on brand.

What you’ll do here

  • Execute regional field marketing plans aligned to global strategy and North America priorities.

  • Run virtual and in-person events that people actually remember, from platform engineering roundtables to developer meetups to enterprise field programs.

  • Produce “better together” reference architectures for strategic partner combinations across cloud providers and AI platforms. Include deployment diagrams, network topology, IAM patterns, and operational runbooks that partner SAs can hand directly to customers.

  • Codify each successful partner engagement into a repeatable GTM play: trigger conditions, discovery questions, positioning framework, demo script, PoV scope template, and expected outcomes. Build a playbook library that a new PDE or partner seller can pick up and run.

  • Build AI-powered self-service tools that automate high-volume PDE activities: Opportunity Brief Generator, PR/FAQ Generator, Workshop-in-a-Box deployment, and demo site builder.

  • Produce a monthly partner intelligence digest from EMEA engagements: what customers are asking for, how competitors are positioning, where integrations are missing, which vertical use cases are emerging. Distribute to Product, Engineering, and GTM leadership.

  • Own the EMEA-relevant portions of the joint technical integration roadmap with strategic partners. Define priorities cross-functionally with Product and Engineering based on field signals from the EMEA market.

  • Create and publish Partner Relations content, the ecosystem equivalent of Developer Relations: technical blog posts, cookbooks, partner ecosystem conference talks, enablement videos, and workshop recaps. Build Coder’s technical brand within the EMEA partner community.

  • Contribute to cloud marketplace product listing stewardship, competency maintenance documentation, and CSP co-build technical requirements as they apply to EMEA-specific partner and compliance contexts.

What We’re Looking For

  • 7+ years of experience in a combination of Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Field CTO, Technical Consulting, or Developer Relations roles at an infrastructure, developer tools, or AI company

  • Demonstrated experience helping partners or customers understand and adopt products in emerging or undefined categories, not just executing playbooks for established ones

  • Proven hands-on experience designing and deploying cloud infrastructure on at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure), with production-level Kubernetes and Terraform depth. You have done the work and can speak to it with specificity.

  • 2+ years deploying or operating AI coding agents in a production or near-production environment: you understand how agent loops execute, where credentials live, and what governance and audit requirements look like in a European enterprise context

  • Ability to articulate the architectural difference between workspace-local agent tooling and a centralized agentic harness, and to explain why that distinction matters to a security, compliance, or data sovereignty stakeholder

  • Experience working with channel or technology partners in a co-sell model: hyperscaler partner programs, GSI/RSI partnerships, or VAR/distributor ecosystems in EMEA markets

  • Experience building repeatable technical GTM assets that scaled beyond your personal delivery: sales plays, enablement curricula, reference architectures, or technical content programs

  • Executive communication and Field CTO credibility: you can hold a technical vision conversation with a partner CTO and a deal-level architecture review with an SE in the same day, in English and ideally at least one additional European language

  • Strong written communication: you can produce a Working Backwards PR/FAQ, a technical architecture document, and a blog post without those being separate skills requiring separate people

  • Self-directed, analytically minded, and comfortable operating with full autonomy. You will define processes that don’t exist, build tools that haven’t been scoped, and create a function from first principles in a new region.

Bonus Points

(Bonus tacos? That’s how we say thanks at Coder. Ask us about it.)

  • Prior Forward Deployed Engineer experience at a platform company (Palantir, Scale AI, frontier AI lab, or equivalent embedded deployment model)

  • Track record of public technical advocacy: blog posts, conference talks, open-source contributions, or developer/partner community engagement

  • Experience with hyperscaler partner programs (e.g., ISV Accelerate, strategic collaboration agreements, co-sell programs) at an operational level

  • Familiarity with European regulatory environments: GDPR, DORA, NIS2, AI Act compliance requirements, and data sovereignty patterns for cloud-native deployments

  • Experience with air-gapped or network-isolated deployments common in European financial services, government, or defense contexts

  • Background in AI governance frameworks, session audit requirements, or SIEM integration for AI workloads

  • Experience with LLM gateway or proxy infrastructure (LiteLLM, OpenRouter, or equivalent) in a multi-team or enterprise context

  • Experience designing human-in-the-loop breakpoints or escalation patterns for autonomous agent workflows

  • Kubernetes certification (CKA, CKAD, or CKS)

  • Experience with Tailscale or similar overlay networking tools

  • Open-source contributions, particularly in CNCF, MCP, or AI agent ecosystems

  • Existing relationships with hyperscaler EMEA solutions architecture teams, European GSI technical practices, or AI infrastructure partner ecosystems

  • Fluency in German, French, or a Nordic language in addition to English

What Success Looks Like

  • You can walk a partner CTO through how Coder enables parallelized AI agents in a regulated European enterprise, covering credential isolation, audit lineage, GDPR-compliant data handling, and escalation design, and turn that conversation into a joint GTM play their sellers can run next quarter.

  • Build repeatable country playbooks so each new market doesn't start from scratch

  • Keep international employee data accurate in Rippling and Deel, and support audits and reporting

  • Strong working knowledge of UK employment law, and familiarity with EOR models and their limitations

  • Hands-on experience with Rippling and/or Deel

  • Comfort working independently across time zones, with early UK-hours overlap and occasional UK travel

  • Detail-oriented enough to catch a contract or comp error before it ships, and strategic enough to know when to escalate

  • Extremely collaborative, working closely with a US- and London-based team

You lead rollouts, monitor health and usage, and keep stakeholders informed. You bring the technical fluency to guide deployment and adoption decisions, connect technical priorities to business outcomes, and engage specialists when deeper expertise is needed. You partner with Sales on expansions and renewals, and with Solutions, Support, Product, and Engineering on implementation, issues, and feedback.

What you’ll do here

  • Own onboarding and rollout plans for new customers; coordinate with Sales and Solutions for a smooth, successful implementation of Coder’s platform.

  • Engage with customers to understand goals, challenges, and use cases, and provide tailored guidance and recommendations.

  • Own the account’s technical success plan: translate customer goals and deployment context into adoption milestones, technical priorities, and a roadmap for broader use of Coder. Align owners and timelines, and track progress against agreed outcomes.

  • Guide customer admins and platform teams on deployment readiness, configuration best practices, and ongoing adoption. Lead technical discovery, facilitate admin enablement, and troubleshoot common adoption blockers; coordinate Solutions, Support, or Engineering for architecture design, complex implementations, and deeper troubleshooting.

  • Identify expansion opportunities within existing accounts, and partner with Sales on upsell and cross-sell motions.

  • Oversee renewals and forecasting, ensuring timely, successful commitments.

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for inquiries, issues, and escalations, and collaborate with Coder teams to resolve them.

  • Monitor and report on customer health and usage, including technical risks and progress toward adoption milestones.

  • Develop deep expertise in Coder’s products to provide global customer coverage.

What we’re looking for

  • 5+ years in customer success or a technical customer-facing role, with experience independently managing enterprise accounts and driving adoption, retention, and expansion.

  • Practical knowledge of cloud infrastructure, DevOps, developer tools, coding agents, platform engineering, CI/CD, and the SDLC; ability to discuss how these fit into a customer’s environment and inform their adoption strategy.

  • Experience guiding customer onboarding and deployments in SaaS or self-hosted environments. Able to understand a deployment architecture, ask informed questions about infrastructure and security, investigate common issues using logs and documentation, and turn findings into clear next steps.

jobs.title: Sales Onboarding Program Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Coder's Revenue Enablement team is building out onboarding and ramp for every customer-facing function — SDR, AE, SE, CSM, and FDE. We're looking for a Sales Onboarding Program Manager who can own that curriculum end to end: designing, running, and continuously improving how new hires ramp from day one to full productivity.

This isn't a single-audience onboarding role. You'll build ramp programs that flex across distinct functions with different skill requirements — commercial, technical, and delivery — while keeping a consistent bar for what "ready" looks like across all of them. You'll work closely with our technical enablement and sales performance functions to make sure ramp content stays current with product, methodology, and process as the company scales.

What you'll do

  • Design and own the onboarding curriculum and certification framework for new hires across AE, SE, CSM, and FDE roles

  • Build structured ramp timelines (30/60/90-day plans) with clear milestones, checkpoints, and certification gates for each function

  • Partner with technical enablement, sales performance, and functional leaders to keep ramp content aligned with current product, methodology (e.g., MEDDPIC, deal qualification frameworks), and sales/delivery process

  • Track and report on ramp metrics — time-to-productivity, certification completion, early performance indicators — and use that data to iterate on the program

  • Coordinate logistics and scheduling for cohort-based onboarding (live sessions, shadowing, certification exercises)

  • Build and maintain a scalable content/documentation system so onboarding materials stay current as the team grows and product evolves

  • Gather feedback from new hires and their managers to continuously refine the program

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for new hires during their ramp period

What we’re looking for

  • 4+ years in program management, enablement, or L&D, ideally in a B2B SaaS or technical sales environment

  • Demonstrated ability to build structured, repeatable programs from scratch — not just run existing ones

  • Strong project management instincts: you default to milestones, checklists, and metrics rather than ad hoc coordination

  • Comfort designing curriculum for both commercial and technical audiences, or a fast learner's willingness to get conversant in technical sales motions
